attributes.title: Preregistration: Block I H1.5 Boundary and Timescale Robustness - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
attributes.description:
This follow-up study tests H1.5 from Experimental Block I of the Theory of Everything Research Programme: whether the principal reciprocal causal maintenance organisation identified in the completed B2 study remains recognisable under reasonable changes of system boundary and temporal resolution.

The primary hypothesis is that the interventionally supported reciprocal component core C1→C2→C3→C1 will remain identifiable under two preregistered boundary descriptions and across three matched disturbance-correlation timescales and four observation intervals. The study does not require the exploratory internal-maintenance fraction chi_int to remain numerically invariant, because changing the system boundary changes whether the common maintenance-resource channel is classified as internal or external.

A Retain verdict requires all three reciprocal edges to remain above preregistered causal-effect thresholds across tau = 1, 4 and 8; persistence of the edge effects and topology selectivity at observation intervals Delta = 1, 5, 10 and 20; invariance of the three-node strongly connected causal core across the core and expanded boundary descriptions; and a preregistered causal effect of the common maintenance-resource channel on all three components.

A positive result supports only robustness of the artificial reciprocal causal maintenance core across the registered representations. It does not overturn the completed B2 finding that reciprocal topology is not established as necessary for artificial maintenance capacity, and it does not establish biological organisational closure, life, metabolism, heredity, intelligence or consciousness.
tags: Theory of Everything Research Programme causal maintenance self-maintenance organisational closure system boundary timescale robustness causal intervention computational simulation

344-2.value:
This study evaluates whether the reciprocal causal maintenance organisation identified in the completed B2 experiment is robust to preregistered changes in system boundary and temporal resolution.

The primary research questions are:

Boundary robustness: Does the interventionally supported reciprocal causal core (C_1 \rightarrow C_2 \rightarrow C_3 \rightarrow C_1) remain identifiable when the system is described using both the preregistered core boundary and the expanded boundary that additionally includes the common maintenance-resource channel?

Disturbance-timescale robustness: Do the three reciprocal maintenance edges remain above the preregistered causal-effect threshold when disturbance correlation timescale is varied across (\tau = 1, 4,) and (8), while integrated disturbance load is held constant?

Observation-resolution robustness: Do the causal edge effects and reciprocal topology remain recognisable when the same underlying trajectories are evaluated at observation intervals (\Delta = 1, 5, 10,) and (20)?

Resource-channel contribution: Does withdrawal of the common maintenance-resource channel produce a preregistered causal deficit in all three organisational components, supporting its functional relevance under the expanded boundary description?

The primary hypothesis, H1.5, is:

H1.5: The principal reciprocal causal maintenance organisation will remain recognisable under reasonable changes of system boundary and temporal resolution.

A Retain verdict requires all three reciprocal edges to remain above the preregistered causal-effect threshold across the three disturbance timescales; preservation of the expected topology across the four observation intervals; invariance of the three-node strongly connected causal core under both boundary descriptions; and demonstration of a causal contribution from the common maintenance-resource channel to all three components.

The hypothesis does not require the exploratory internal-maintenance fraction (\chi_{\mathrm{int}}) to remain numerically invariant across boundary descriptions. A change in (\chi_{\mathrm{int}}) is expected when the common maintenance-resource channel changes classification from external to internal. The decisive question is whether the underlying causal maintenance organisation remains identifiable.

A positive result would support robustness of the artificial reciprocal causal maintenance core only within the registered architecture family, boundaries and timescales. It would not establish that reciprocal topology is necessary for artificial self-maintenance, nor would it establish biological organisational closure, life, metabolism, heredity, intelligence or consciousness.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value: No H1.5 confirmatory data exist. Twenty held-out seeds have been registered but not executed. Three development-only seeds were used to validate the robustness implementation and set pilot-informed thresholds. Those pilot data are excluded from confirmatory evidence. The pilot established that integrated disturbance load can be preserved while temporal correlation is varied, that all three reciprocal edges can be measured interventionally, and that chi_int changes when the common resource channel crosses the chosen system boundary. The confirmatory manifests, seeds, boundaries, temporal scales, thresholds and decision rules were frozen before registration, and software execution is gated until the registration is public.

value: Simulation study: Using existing or synthetic data to assess performance of a model, mimic operation of an existing or proposed system, or predict possible outcomes in a controlled context. This may include demonstration of methods, many varieties of modeling, prediction of policy impacts, simulating behavior or outcomes in a population, and other designs.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.

344-38.value: No blinding is used because the study is a deterministic/controlled-stochastic computational simulation with automated quantitative analysis. Researcher flexibility is constrained by frozen manifests, twenty held-out seeds, fixed boundary definitions, fixed temporal scales, fixed edge thresholds, automated provenance checks and a preregistered decision rule. Any post-confirmatory analysis not specified in this record will be labelled exploratory.

344-40.value:
This is a paired computational intervention study of one reciprocal three-component maintenance architecture. At each disturbance-correlation scale tau in {1,4,8}, the same twenty seeds are run under intact reciprocal maintenance and under targeted ablation of C1, C2 and C3. An additional tau=1 condition withdraws the common maintenance-resource channel from step 200 onward. All trajectories run to step 600.

For each seed, the fine-grained disturbance sequence is generated once from the registered RNG procedure. For tau>1, each contiguous tau-step block is replaced by its component-wise mean, preserving exact integrated disturbance load within the block while changing temporal correlation. Edge effects are evaluated at terminal state and over post-ablation observations sampled at Delta in {1,5,10,20}.

Boundary robustness is assessed without changing the executable trajectory. Under B_core, C1,C2,C3 are internal and the common resource channel R is external. Under B_expanded, R is included within the system description. The primary boundary question is whether the same interventionally supported C1-C2-C3 strongly connected component survives both descriptions.

344-44.value: No subjects or experimental units are randomly assigned to conditions. Twenty explicit confirmatory seeds are preregistered and reused across matched conditions for paired comparison. The seed set is disjoint from all development and original B2 confirmatory seeds.

344-47.value: New computational data will be generated only after the registration is public and the execution gate is opened. The sampling frame is the fixed set of twenty preregistered seeds crossed with thirteen frozen confirmatory conditions. Raw trajectories, seed identities, component states, disturbances, maintenance actions, intervention labels, configuration hashes and provenance records are archived automatically.

344-51.value: There are twenty independent confirmatory seed identities. Thirteen conditions are planned: four conditions at each of three disturbance timescales (12 condition-level runs per seed) plus one reference-timescale resource-withdrawal condition. The design therefore contains 260 planned seed-by-condition simulation runs. Repeated simulation steps within a seed/condition run are nested observations, not independent replicates.

344-53.value: Twenty seeds were fixed prospectively to provide substantially greater replication than the three-seed development pilot and to permit preregistered consistency criteria of 16/20 seeds while keeping the small interpretable system computationally inexpensive. Sample size will not be increased because a confirmatory result is borderline or unfavourable.

344-55.value: Development ended after the three-seed pilot validated the implementation and informed the frozen thresholds. Confirmatory data collection begins only after public preregistration and formal execution-gate clearance. Data collection ends when all thirteen conditions have valid runs for all twenty seeds, subject only to documented reruns of technically invalid runs using the same registered seed. There is no outcome-dependent early stopping and no addition of new seeds in response to observed results.

344-58.value: None, in the OSF randomisation-specific sense. No random assignment is used. Prospectively specified simulation conditions vary disturbance-correlation scale, targeted node ablation and common-resource availability.

344-62.value: Measured variables include C1, C2 and C3 state at each simulation step; viability status; disturbance vector; internal and external maintenance actions; total maintenance expenditure; intervention status; seed identity; and complete provenance/integrity metadata. Derived confirmatory quantities include terminal component states, intact-minus-ablated downstream edge effects, topology selectivity, post-ablation window edge effects at four sampling intervals, common-resource withdrawal effects, retained causal graph edges, strongly connected component structure and exploratory chi_int under two boundary classifications.

344-66.value: For edge Ci→Cj, terminal effect is q_j,intact(T) - q_j,ablated(i)(T). Topology selectivity is the expected-target deficit minus the deficit in the other non-ablated component. Post-ablation window quantities use the same definitions averaged over registered observations from step 250 through 600 at Delta = 1, 5, 10 or 20. The common-resource effect on Cj is q_j,intact(T) - q_j,resource-withdrawn(T). chi_int is calculated from positive component-edge and resource-support effects under each boundary classification, but it is descriptive and is not required to be invariant.

344-71.value: No fitted parametric model is used for the primary decision. Primary inference uses paired effect estimates, seed-level consistency counts and the frozen quantitative thresholds. Paired percentile-bootstrap 95% intervals with 10,000 resamples and fixed analysis RNG seed 20261004 are reported for continuous paired effects. Graph structure is reconstructed from intervention-sensitive edges exceeding the preregistered threshold epsilon_w=0.25.

344-75.value: No outcome-dependent transformation is used. Temporal robustness uses preregistered subsampling intervals Delta = 1,5,10,20. Disturbance timescale tau>1 is generated by blockwise component-wise averaging of a common fine-grained disturbance schedule, preserving integrated disturbance load. Component states remain on their native [0,1] scale.

344-77.value: Retain requires all six criteria stated in the formal preregistration PDF: all three mean terminal edge effects >0.25 at each tau; at least 16/20 seed-level terminal effects >=0.20 per edge/tau; all post-ablation mean effects >=0.25 and mean selectivities >=0.18 for every edge/tau/Delta; at least 16/20 seed-level window effects >=0.20 and selectivities >=0.12; the same three-node strongly connected causal core under both registered boundaries; and mean common-resource withdrawal effect >=0.25 on each component. Restrict, Reduce, Suspend and Reject follow the formal frozen definitions. No multiple-significance-testing correction is used because primary inference is threshold/architecture based rather than a family of null-hypothesis significance tests.

344-79.value: All valid registered runs are included. No scientific outlier rule is used. A run is excluded only for preregistered technical invalidity such as hash mismatch, wrong seed, non-finite state, environment failure, corrupted required output or failed provenance. Invalid runs remain in the audit trail and may be rerun with the same seed.

344-81.value: No imputation is planned. A technically incomplete run is INVALID_RUN and may be rerun with the same registered seed after correction. If decisive evidence cannot be completed validly, the appropriate conclusion is Suspend rather than imputation or silent deletion.

344-83.value: Exploratory reporting may include chi_int under the two boundary descriptions, detailed time-series visualisation and descriptive comparison of edge-effect trajectories. These analyses cannot replace a failed primary criterion. Any additional boundary, disturbance timescale, observation interval or graph metric introduced after confirmatory outcomes are observed will be labelled exploratory or separately preregistered.

344-86.value: This study completes the only primary Block I hypothesis deliberately deferred from the preregistered B2 causal-maintenance study. It is a robustness test, not a new claim that reciprocal closure is necessary. Even if H1.5 is retained, B2 H1.6 remains reduced unless a separate future study supplies new evidence against the successful bypass architecture.
